## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

1. **`install.sh` §4b digests SOURCE bytes for components the installer's own preservation policy is designed NOT to overwrite, permanently bricking lint provisioning and hard-failing the whole cloud implement job.** §4b (`install.sh:1531-1563`) passes `--repo-root "$SRC"` and digests source-tree bytes for `setup-action`, `provision-helper`, `implement-workflow` and `manifest`, recording their consumer runtime paths. But `install_managed` (`install.sh:687`) PRESERVES a `modified` / `unverified` / `unreadable` artifact and writes the new version to a `.prflow-new` sidecar; and the workflow copy loop is skipped entirely when `tier1_rc != 0` while §4b still records the source digest of `devflow-implement.yml`. `check_readiness` then returns `digest-mismatch:<name>` and `provision-lint-tools.sh` `_die`s — a hard `exit 1` inside a step of `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-project-env` with no `continue-on-error`, so the **entire `/prflow:implement` job fails**, not merely lint provisioning. Three routine non-adversarial paths reach it: a consumer who hand-edited `devflow-implement.yml` or the setup action (which `CLAUDE.md` calls "ordinary work, not maintainer-only" and which install.sh itself advertises a sidecar-merge workflow for); any pre-manifest installation upgrading (every differing artifact classifies `unverified` → preserved); and a Tier-1 migration refusal. The emitted remedy — `re-run the PRFlow installer (install.sh) so the marker matches the installed components` — cannot resolve it: re-running preserves the same bytes and re-records the same source digest, so the loop never converges. The fix is to digest the INSTALLED (consumer, `--repo-root .`) bytes, or to refuse to publish a marker naming a component this run preserved or skipped. This is also the repository's own named `unverified-assumption` class inverted: the guard's comparand comes from a producer that does not emit it on every path the guard now selects. (raised by 4/6 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out: install.sh]

2. **`hardensetup` is a fourth displaced-path producer that publishes no disclosure, so the reviewing agent reads base-ref bytes as if they were head — on exactly the file a PR editing that action would be under review for.** `devflow-runner.yml`'s `displaced_join` (line 2078) joins THREE declared producers — `harden_hooks.outputs.displaced_paths`, `promptext.outputs.truncated_paths`, `harden_guard.outputs.guard_paths` — into `HARDENED_PATHS`, which the grounding block renders and Phase 0.1.5 writes to `.prflow/tmp/displaced-paths.txt`; Phases 2, 3 and 4.1.6 then route those paths through `git show <head>:<path>` instead of a working-tree read. The new `hardensetup` step (line 1405) overwrites every base-ref file of `.github/actions/setup-project-env/` over the workspace copy and `rm -f`s any PR-added file there, sets NO step output, and is absent from `displaced_join`'s env — while running at line 1405, well before `displaced_join`, so it could publish. That same workflow states the governing contract inline: *"the disclosure is what stops a reviewing agent reading this step's rewritten bytes as untouched PR-head content — that is the case this producer exists for."* The added `#1388 hardensetup` tests pin the displacement behavior and assert nothing about the disclosure. (raised by 1/6 agents — single-source, flagged for extra scrutiny; the orchestrator independently confirmed the three-producer join and hardensetup's absence from it) [.github/workflows/devflow-runner.yml:1404-1443]

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. The `provision-lint-tools.sh` readiness-refusal remedy string — `remedy: re-run the PRFlow installer (install.sh) so the marker matches the installed components` — is a diff-added command-form that is false against HEAD for the dominant `digest-mismatch` cause (a preserved local edit): re-running reproduces the identical marker and preserves the edit again, yielding the identical refusal. The true remedy is to merge the `.prflow-new` sidecar or restore the shipped bytes first. (raised by 2/6 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out: .github/actions/setup-project-env/provision-lint-tools.sh]

2. The `TOOLS` comment states a property the code does not implement: `TOOLS must stay a function of the manifest's tool set: the cross-run cache key does not include it, so an out-of-manifest tool would ride a partial cache restore.` `TOOLS="${TOOLS:-shellcheck ruff}"` is a hardcoded literal with no manifest read anywhere in its derivation — a third independent copy of the tool set beside `lint_manifest.KNOWN_TOOLS` and `lint_provision.KNOWN_TOOLS`. And an out-of-manifest tool does not ride a cache restore: an unknown tool takes the rc-4 `_die` arm and a manifest-declared tool with no artifact takes rc 3 and degrades. A maintainer reading this believes a fail-open hazard exists that the code fails closed on, and could "fix" it by loosening the real refusal. (raised by 2/6 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out: .github/actions/setup-project-env/provision-lint-tools.sh]

3. The vendored readers are bound by an install-time digest at `$pin` but resolved at RUN time from a ref `install.sh` may not control. `devflow_pin_version` KEEPS an existing deliberate pin (`kept existing prflow_version in $cfg … not overwriting.`) and `install.sh:1686-1688` falls back to `PIN="$REF"` (possibly a mutable branch) in the curl-piped case. In either case the vendor fetch materializes helper bytes at a different commit than the marker digested, producing `digest-mismatch:manifest-reader` — the same hard, non-converging refusal as Critical 1, on a repo where nothing is wrong. The `install_state.py` docstring's "identical bytes at the pinned ref" premise does not hold. (raised by 2/6 agents) [install.sh:1533-1553]

4. `install_state.build_state` does not close the round trip its own docstring promises. The docstring says it raises `ValueError` for anything `validate_state` would later reject "so the installer fails BEFORE publishing a marker that binds a file it cannot read or that provisioning will refuse" — but that holds for `installer_version` only. Component NAMES and recorded PATHS are copied through unchecked: `build_state('v1.0', {'My_Comp': 'scripts/lint_manifest.py'})` builds fine while `validate_state` rejects it with `invalid-value: component name 'My_Comp'` (confirmed by execution). `main`'s `build` takes NAME from `--component NAME=PATH` verbatim, so an installer passing an underscored or capitalised name writes a marker, exits 0, and every later `verify` fails closed on the consumer — at provisioning time, not publication time. One line of reuse fixes it: run the assembled dict through `validate_state` before returning. (raised by 1/6 agents) [scripts/install_state.py:257-282]

5. `Plan.__init__(status, **kw)` silently absorbs unknown keywords, and `tool`/`os`/`arch` are required on NO status. Nothing rejects a key outside the two fixed name lists, so a misspelled field is a silently `None` attribute (`Plan("unsupported", reason="x", tooll="typo", os="linux").tool -> None`, confirmed by execution). `main`'s `cache-key` path feeds `plan.os, plan.arch, plan.tool` straight into `cache_key`, so an under-populated plan yields a well-formed-looking key containing the literal `None` — exactly the "stale binary satisfies a changed tuple" failure `cache_key`'s own docstring says the key exists to prevent. Latent today (every `build_plan` return site passes all three), but enforced by caller convention precisely where the sibling types enforce it in the constructor; `__slots__` already declares the closed field set, so the check is cheap. (raised by 1/6 agents) [scripts/lint_provision.py:131-156]

6. The `SCRIPTS_DIR` fallback in `action.yml` has no third arm verifying the chosen directory actually contains the helpers: it probes only `lint_provision.py` while `provision-lint-tools.sh` also invokes `$SCRIPTS_DIR/install_state.py`. If neither directory exists, python exits non-zero with `can't open file …` and the script reports `install-state readiness refused: <traceback> — remedy: re-run the PRFlow installer`, a wrong-cause diagnosis of a missing helper whose real remedy is repairing the vendor materialization. This is the error class `install_managed`'s own `unreadable` arm goes to lengths to avoid. (raised by 2/6 agents) [.github/actions/setup-project-env/action.yml:264-285]

7. The base-ref hardening step drives a DESTRUCTIVE selection through `grep`, a non-preflight PATH tool, and discards the fetch failure's cause. `printf '%s\n' "${base_files[@]}" | grep -qxF "$head_f" || rm -f "$head_f"` puts the `grep` result on the left of `||`, so `set -e`/`pipefail` cannot fire: a missing or failing `grep` makes EVERY head file take the `rm -f` arm. The job does still abort — but only incidentally, via the next line's `[ -f "$dir/action.yml" ]` check, and with a message (`base ref carries no action.yml`) that misattributes the cause. Separately, line 1415 sends the fetch's stderr to `/dev/null` and reports only "could not fetch base ref", discarding the whole diagnostic (auth, shallow clone, unknown ref) on a security-critical fail-closed arm. `CLAUDE.md` names this class explicitly: a value determining a selection or an emitted result must not be derived through a non-preflight PATH tool. (raised by 1/6 agents) [.github/workflows/devflow-runner.yml:1415-1441]

8. The compatibility tuple is transcribed TWICE with nothing reconciling the copies, so the completeness the whole feature rests on is unenforced. `lib/generate-install-state.py`'s `COMPONENTS` (7 entries) and `install.sh` §4b's `--component` operand list are independent literal copies, plus a `--record-path` mapping that exists only in `install.sh`. Add a component to `COMPONENTS` and forget `install.sh` and every CONSUMER's marker silently binds a weaker tuple, while both the drift gate (`--check`, repo-local) and the 4b end-to-end tests stay green; the reciprocal error is equally invisible. A test parsing the `--component`/`--record-path` operands out of `install.sh` and asserting key-set equality with `COMPONENTS` catches both directions. **This is also the Phase 3.1.5 completeness critic's own finding — see the critic note below.** (raised by 2/6 agents) [lib/generate-install-state.py:36-44]

9. `#1388`'s `structural-pin-ok` declaration on a log-prose literal. `"no lint-tool provisioning and no manifest validation" in _ACTION_1388` is declared `# structural-pin-ok: routing-dispatch-contract`, but the protected literal is the body of an `echo` at `action.yml:255` — human log prose no tool consumes; the actual routing decision is the `case` structure, already covered by the separate `lint_mode:` input and `unknown lint_mode` refusal pins. Rewording that echo turns the suite RED with no behavior change. Per this repository's review extension, a newly added wording-only / documentation-presence pin is at least Important unless it carries a VALID declaration, and `a # structural-pin-ok: comment does not make prose executable`. Replace with the executable step-body assertion recommended below. (raised by 2/6 agents) [lib/test/test_python_scripts.py:37270]

10. The composite action's lint-provisioning step body has ZERO executable coverage. `action.yml`'s ~250-285 block holds real decision logic — the closed `lint_mode` case, the `RUNNER_OS`→`TARGET_OS` and `RUNNER_ARCH`→`TARGET_ARCH` mapping tables, and the `SCRIPTS_DIR` fallback — all covered only by substring pins on file text. Those mapping tables are an unreconciled mirror of `lint_provision.KNOWN_OS`/`KNOWN_ARCH`: a typo makes every arm64 runner exit 1, or maps to a tuple that degrades instead of provisioning, and no test moves. This PR already demonstrates the right technique on `hardensetup` (extract the `run` block from the YAML, execute it against a fixture); apply it here. (raised by 1/6 agents) [.github/actions/setup-project-env/action.yml:250-285]

11. The `GITHUB_PATH` export — the step that makes provisioning observable to the model — is never exercised. `_run_helper_1388` does `env.pop("GITHUB_PATH", None)`, so the `if [ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ]` append at `provision-lint-tools.sh:246-248` runs in NO test. Delete that block or write the wrong value and every fail-closed arm still passes while the implement tier's model never sees `shellcheck`/`ruff` on PATH — the exact silent degradation this feature exists to prevent. One assertion on an existing happy-path fixture closes it. (raised by 1/6 agents) [.github/actions/setup-project-env/provision-lint-tools.sh:246-248]

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor

1. `tar.xz` — the archive type EVERY real shellcheck artifact uses — is never extracted in a test. `_mk_archive_1388` builds only `tar.gz`, and the one non-gz case is `zip`, so the production extraction path (`tar -xf` on xz, needing xz support in whatever `tar` the runner ships) is exercised nowhere. [lib/test/test_python_scripts.py]
2. The drift gate has no RED-direction test: the suite asserts `--check` exits 0 on the current tree, so an inverted comparison or an unset `check` would leave the gate inert and nothing would say so. [lib/generate-install-state.py:82-100]
3. The multi-tool loop is never run — every `_run_helper_1388` call passes `tools="shellcheck"` while production `TOOLS` defaults to `"shellcheck ruff"`, leaving `PROVISIONED`/`UNPROVISIONED` accumulation and the tool-1-succeeds/tool-2-fails ordering untested. [provision-lint-tools.sh:241-256]
4. The §4b positive control asserts structural validity (`load_state(...).status == "established"`), never readiness (`check_readiness(...).ready`) against the consumer tree — which is precisely what would have caught Critical 1. [lib/test/modules/installer-wiring.sh]
5. The unwritable-target fixture chmods a parent to `0o555` with no `os.geteuid() != 0` guard, inconsistent with two sibling permission fixtures in the same file that DO guard on root; under uid 0 the `mkdir` succeeds and the assertion fails loudly rather than silently — an environment-dependent RED with no attribution. [lib/test/test_python_scripts.py:36921-36930]
6. Nothing verifies the pinned digests against upstream reality. This PR is the proof: the linux/x86_64 shellcheck digest on `main` was WRONG and would have hard-failed provisioning on every real runner while the whole suite stayed green, because every test computes its own fixture digest. A periodic network-permitted re-derivation job is the only thing that catches this class. [.prflow/lint-manifest.json]

## Phase 3.1.5 — completeness-critic pass (forced: `detect_all_audit` is set)

1. **Target population and property.** The audit under introduction is `lib/generate-install-state.py`'s `COMPONENTS` map plus its `--check` drift gate. It claims to cover *every component whose bytes must agree for lint provisioning to be safe*, and asserts a completeness property over that whole set (the marker binds each one by sha256; provisioning refuses on any skew).
2. **Independent re-enumeration.** I derived the population by a signal other than the audit's own list: the module import graph (`install_state.py` and `lint_provision.py` each `spec_from_file_location("lint_manifest", …)`) plus the invocation graph read out of `action.yml` and `provision-lint-tools.sh` (`$SCRIPTS_DIR/install_state.py`, `$SCRIPTS_DIR/lint_provision.py`, `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/provision-lint-tools.sh`, `.prflow/lint-manifest.json`, `.prflow/install-state.json`), plus every workflow passing `lint_mode` (`grep -rn 'lint_mode' .github/workflows/`).
3. **Superset assertion.** The audit's set IS a superset of that independent enumeration. The only members outside it are `devflow.yml` and `devflow-runner.yml`, which pass `lint_mode: none` and therefore run no provisioning and validate no manifest — a defensible exclusion, not a gap.
4. **BUT the critic surfaces one finding the superset test does not.** The population is enumerated TWICE — once as `COMPONENTS` in `lib/generate-install-state.py` and once as `install.sh` §4b's `--component`/`--record-path` operands — and nothing reconciles the two. The `--check` drift gate therefore certifies completeness only with respect to the REPO-LOCAL copy and is structurally blind to the CONSUMER copy, which is the one the whole feature ships. That is the classic self-certifying-audit shape, and it is filed as Important 8 above (corroborated by `pr-test-analyzer` independently).

## Phase 4.1.5 — over-grade advisory annotations and the behavior-inert prose cap

**Cap applied (deterministic, changes the severity)** to Suggestions 11, 12 and 16 — findings whose subject is a sentence in `docs/internal/**` or a module docstring. Limb one (no tool reads it for behavior): enumerated the readers — no lint, parser, codegen sentinel or declaration marker under `lib/test/` parses these surfaces to decide behavior; a suite pin that merely asserts the prose does not make it non-inert. Limb two (no consumer reads it): `docs/internal/**` is pruned by the vendor slice and ships to no consumer, and the `install_state.py` docstring is not rendered to any user. Both limbs hold, so each is capped at 🟡 Suggestion and drives no REJECT at the `critical` threshold.

**Cap NOT applied** to Important 1 and Important 2, and to Critical 1's `plain cp` premise. Limb two fails for each: `provision-lint-tools.sh`'s remedy string is rendered to a consumer operator in their own Actions log, and `install.sh` is downloaded and read by consumers. Each is therefore a self-contradicting-diff carve-out finding and REJECTs non-demotably. Their carve-out markers appear on the finding lines above.

**Advisory-only annotations (never change the verdict):**
- Critical 2 — `[suspected over-grade: shape 3 — uncorroborated single-source finding]`. It is single-source from the final-pass reviewer. The annotation is advisory ONLY; the orchestrator independently confirmed both operands (the three-producer `displaced_join` at line 2078 and `hardensetup`'s absence from it), so the finding stands at Critical.
- Important 7 — `[suspected over-grade: shape 1 — the observable fail-direction is fail-closed (the next line's action.yml existence check aborts the job), milder than the Important label]`. Advisory only; the finding stands, because the repository names non-preflight-tool-driven selection as its own defect class and the misattributed diagnostic is the real harm.

**Refuted findings (recorded, not filed):**
- `code-reviewer` filed as Critical that the changed shellcheck `linux/x86_64` digest was hand-edited, inferring tampering from the 60-of-64 shared hex prefix between the old and new values. **REFUTED by orchestrator-executed probe:** I downloaded the upstream artifact and computed sha256 — the NEW value is correct and the value on `main` was wrong. `pr-test-analyzer` and the final-pass reviewer each independently downloaded and reached the same conclusion. This PR FIXES a bad pin.
- A checklist item proposed falsifying `cloud-setup.md`'s "no PR-head bytes ever enter the review job" via a repo with `provision_env` off. **REFUTED:** `hardensetup` and the `uses:` step carry the identical `if:` gate (VC-48 PASS).

## Phase 4.1.6 — pre-verdict truthfulness sweep

Promoted into the self-contradicting-diff carve-out: Important 1 (the false remedy string) and Important 2 (the `TOOLS` comment). Both are diff-added artifacts whose claims were demonstrated false against HEAD by reading the code path each describes, and neither is covered by the 4.1.5 cap. Critical 1 carries the same routing for its `plain cp` premise.

intra-diff contradiction scan: one contradicting pair found — the `provision-lint-tools.sh` header's absolute `Every INTEGRITY failure fails CLOSED naming the tool` against the same file's `_die -` readiness arm (the same symbol, the same file, the same diff). Filed as checklist FAIL VC-25 and reflected in Important 1's neighbourhood; it routes into the carve-out rather than being capped, because `provision-lint-tools.sh` ships to consumers and its diagnostics are read by a consumer operator.

## Verdict Criteria
- Any FAIL in verification checklist → REJECT — **7 FAILs (VC-24, VC-25, VC-36, VC-37, VC-50, VC-55, VC-66); rule 1 fires.**
- Any INCONCLUSIVE → REJECT — none.
- Self-contradicting-diff carve-out (non-demotable, threshold-independent) → REJECT — **fires on Critical 1, Important 1 and Important 2.**
- Any review-agent finding at or above `critical` (the resolved `prflow_review.verdict_severity_threshold`) → REJECT — **fires on Critical 1 and Critical 2.**
- 2+ review agents failed → not applicable; 6 of 6 dispatched agents returned results.
- Checklist generation failed → no; `checklist_skipped` is `null` (`engine_self_modifying` forced the full checklist).

**Verdict: REJECT.** The acceptance criteria are all met and the Python core is unusually well built — typed XOR-at-construction verdicts, frozen instances, a genuinely adversarial six-shape input matrix, real end-to-end drives of the shell helper and of the shipped `hardensetup` step, and a supply-chain pin correction that this review independently confirmed against upstream. The blocking defects are all outside the happy path: a compatibility marker that binds source-tree digests to files the installer's own preservation policy guarantees will sometimes differ (hard-failing the whole cloud implement job on three ordinary upgrade paths, with a remedy message that cannot resolve it), and a new base-ref displacer that does not disclose itself on a workflow whose established contract is that every displacer does.

phase3_findings.description: install.sh section 4b digests SOURCE bytes for setup-action, provision-helper, implement-workflow and manifest while recording consumer runtime paths, but install_managed PRESERVES a modified/unverified/unreadable artifact (sidecar .prflow-new) and the tier1_rc != 0 arm skips the workflow copy loop entirely. check_readiness then returns digest-mismatch and provision-lint-tools.sh _die's, hard-failing the whole cloud implement job permanently, with a printed remedy (re-run the installer) that cannot converge.

Same defect: the marker binds SOURCE digests for components install.sh may deliberately preserve or skip, so a supported install outcome hard-fails every later implement run with a non-remedy. The guard's comparand comes from a producer that does not emit it on every path the guard now selects.

Same defect, with the availability consequence traced: the _die is a hard exit 1 inside a step of `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-project-env` with no continue-on-error, so the entire /prflow:implement job fails. Three routine non-adversarial paths reach it (hand-edited workflow or action; pre-manifest installation upgrading, where every differing artifact classifies unverified; plugin auto-update replacing the vendored readers).

The new hardensetup step displaces PR-head bytes for .github/actions/setup-project-env/ but publishes no displaced_paths output and is absent from displaced_join's three-producer env, so HARDENED_PATHS omits it and the reviewing agent reads base-ref bytes from the working tree as if they were head — on exactly the file a PR editing that action would be under review for. That workflow states the governing contract inline for its other producers.

The readiness-refusal remedy string 'remedy: re-run the PRFlow installer (install.sh) so the marker matches the installed components' is false against HEAD for the dominant digest-mismatch cause (a preserved local edit): re-running reproduces the identical marker and preserves the edit again. Self-contradicting-diff carve-out.

The TOOLS comment states a consequence the code does not produce: TOOLS is a hardcoded literal, not a function of the manifest, and an out-of-manifest tool cannot ride a partial cache restore (rc-4 hard refusal / rc-3 degrade). A maintainer could 'fix' a hazard that does not exist by loosening the real refusal. Self-contradicting-diff carve-out.

TOOLS is a third independent copy of the tool set beside lint_manifest.KNOWN_TOOLS and lint_provision.KNOWN_TOOLS, with no mechanical link; a manifest declaring a tool this list omits would have that tool silently never provisioned while the readiness gate still said READY.

Vendored helper components are bound by install-time digest at $pin but resolved at run time from a ref install.sh may not control: devflow_pin_version keeps an existing deliberate pin, and install.sh falls back to PIN=$REF (possibly a mutable branch) in the curl-piped case. The 'identical bytes at the pinned ref' comment is false against HEAD.

build_state does not close the round trip its docstring promises: component names and recorded paths are copied through unchecked, so a marker that validate_state later rejects is published successfully and the failure surfaces at provisioning time on the consumer rather than at publication time. Confirmed by execution.

Plan.__init__(status, **kw) silently absorbs unknown keywords and requires tool/os/arch on no status, so a misspelled field is a silently None attribute and an under-populated established plan yields a cache_key containing the literal None — the exact stale-binary failure cache_key exists to prevent. Confirmed by execution.

The SCRIPTS_DIR fallback has no third arm verifying the chosen directory contains the helpers (it probes only lint_provision.py while the helper also invokes install_state.py), so a failed vendor materialization is misreported as a marker-readiness failure and sends the operator to the wrong remedy.

The hardening step drives a destructive rm -f selection through grep, a non-preflight PATH tool, on the left of ||, so set -e/pipefail cannot fire and a missing grep deletes every trusted file just materialized; the job aborts only incidentally via the next existence check, with a misattributed message. The fetch's stderr is also discarded on a security-critical fail-closed arm.

The compatibility tuple is transcribed twice — COMPONENTS in lib/generate-install-state.py and install.sh section 4b's --component operands — with nothing reconciling the copies, so a component added to one side silently narrows every consumer's marker while both the drift gate and the 4b end-to-end tests stay green. Corroborated by the Phase 3.1.5 completeness critic.

Completeness critic: the audit's COMPONENTS set is a superset of an independently derived enumeration (import graph + action/helper invocation graph + lint_mode-passing workflows), so it is complete with respect to that signal. But the population is enumerated twice with no reconciliation, so the --check drift gate certifies completeness only for the repo-local copy and is structurally blind to the consumer copy the feature ships.

A structural-pin-ok declaration covers a log message, not a contract: the pinned literal 'no lint-tool provisioning and no manifest validation' is the body of an echo in action.yml consumed by no tool, declared routing-dispatch-contract. Rewording it turns the suite RED with no behavior change. Per the repo review extension this is a wording-only pin and at least Important.

The composite action's lint-provisioning step body has zero executable coverage: the closed lint_mode case, the RUNNER_OS/RUNNER_ARCH mapping tables (an unreconciled mirror of lint_provision.KNOWN_OS/KNOWN_ARCH), and the SCRIPTS_DIR fallback are covered only by substring pins on file text.

The GITHUB_PATH export is never exercised — _run_helper_1388 pops GITHUB_PATH from the environment, so the append that makes the provisioned tools visible to the model runs in no test; deleting it leaves every fail-closed arm green while the model never sees shellcheck/ruff on PATH.
tar.xz — the archive type every real shellcheck artifact uses — is never extracted in a test; _mk_archive_1388 builds only tar.gz and the one non-gz case is zip.
The drift gate has no RED-direction test: the suite only asserts --check exits 0 on the current tree, so an inverted comparison would leave the gate inert and nothing would say so.

The multi-tool loop is never run: every fixture passes tools=shellcheck while production TOOLS defaults to 'shellcheck ruff', leaving PROVISIONED/UNPROVISIONED accumulation and the partial-failure ordering untested.

The section 4b positive control asserts structural validity (load_state status established), never readiness (check_readiness ready) against the consumer tree — which is exactly what would have caught the Critical marker-skew defect.

The unwritable-target fixture chmods a parent to 0o555 with no os.geteuid() != 0 guard, inconsistent with two sibling permission fixtures in the same file that do guard on root; under uid 0 it is an environment-dependent RED with no attribution.

Nothing verifies the pinned digests against upstream reality — every test computes its own fixture digest, so the wrong pin on main would have hard-failed provisioning on every real runner while the suite stayed green. A periodic network-permitted re-derivation job is the only check for this class.

generate-install-state.py raises untyped tracebacks where every sibling reader returns a typed reason (unguarded json.loads of .prflow/config.json), and main silently ignores unrecognized argv, so a typo like --chek writes the marker instead of checking it.

Section 4b's outer guard has no else arm, so a source tree missing the manifest or install_state.py installs no manifest and no marker, prints nothing, and exits 0 — the only silent arm in a block where every other refusal logs a warning naming its cause.

All four new types leave __delattr__ unguarded and expose their payload by reference, so `del r.state` yields established==True with state unreachable — the shape the constructor works hardest to make unrepresentable — and a certified payload can be mutated in place after certification.
StateResult('established', ...) checks only that state is not None, so it accepts a payload validate_state would refuse (e.g. an empty components object). Holds today by call-site discipline only.

cloud-setup.md's fail-closed list groups readiness reasons with per-tool ones and closes 'each naming the tool', but the readiness gate fires before any tool is selected and emits through _die - . Behavior-inert prose cap applied (both limbs hold: docs/internal is unread by tools and pruned from the vendor slice).

install.md tells consumers their marker is regenerated by lib/generate-install-state.py; that helper's own docstring scopes itself to the primary repo's committed copy and hardcodes _REPO_ROOT, so from a vendored copy it would resolve to the vendor tree. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.

install_state.py's docstring names COMPONENTS in lib/generate-install-state.py as the authoritative set, but the consumer publication path (install.sh section 4b) never consults it. The two agree today; the parenthetical presents one as authoritative for a path it does not govern. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.

The release note's 'can never execute a setup action edited in the pull request under review' is narrowly true of setup-project-env only; read-project-config and vendor-plugin remain PR-head-resolved in the same runner. VC-54 graded the scoped wording accurate, so this stays a clarity Suggestion rather than a promoted falsehood.

Added comment blocks exceed the prevention-only three-line cap and carry derivation rather than the wrong change they prevent: devflow-runner.yml:1393-1403 (11 lines), ci.yml:73-79 (7 lines), and provision-lint-tools.sh's cache/re-verification (6) and pre-provisioned-reuse (4) comments.

The new lint-manifest job was inserted between the jobs-level comment block describing the shard partition and the shard job it documents, so that comment now heads the wrong job and shard: is left undocumented. Capped at Suggestion in the report (organizational, behavior-inert workflow comment).

A missing unzip/tar on a Windows Git Bash or minimal self-hosted runner hard-fails the whole implement job, in tension with the CLAUDE.md convention this same PR adds (reserve fail-closed for integrity checks). AC10 lists 'missing installer primitive' among the fail-closed arms, so the two statements now disagree in-tree.

_die bypasses the RETURN trap (exit 1 does not run a RETURN trap), leaking the mktemp -d work directory on every fail-closed arm. Cosmetic on an ephemeral runner; the suite does drive the helper repeatedly in one process.

REFUTED — filed as Critical that the changed shellcheck linux/x86_64 digest was hand-edited (inferred from the 60-of-64 shared hex prefix between old and new). The orchestrator downloaded shellcheck-v0.10.0.linux.x86_64.tar.xz and ruff-0.6.9-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz from upstream and computed sha256: the NEW values are correct and the value on main was wrong. pr-test-analyzer and the final-pass reviewer independently downloaded and reached the same conclusion. This PR FIXES a bad supply-chain pin. Not filed as a finding.
